create.name: Lisa Ernst
create.bio:
Lisa Ernst is an insight meditation teacher in Nashville, Tennessee, and the founder and guiding teacher of One Dharma Nashville. She spent roughly a decade practising Zen before turning to vipassana and the Thai Forest style associated with Ajahn Chah, and she was later fully authorised to teach by Trudy Goodman in the Spirit Rock lineage of Jack Kornfield. Over three decades of practice she has led retreats and classes at Spirit Rock, Big Bear and Southern Dharma and at InsightLA in Los Angeles, and has guided pilgrimages to India and Costa Rica.

Her teaching blends steady attention to breath and body with open awareness, compassion and lovingkindness, and she is drawn to helping students stay with open, unanswerable questions rather than rushing to solve them. Most Monday evenings she leads meditation, a talk and discussion for the One Dharma community at the Friends meeting house in Nashville, with a Zoom link for those further away. She also runs silent residential retreats at Bethany Hills in Kingston Springs and elsewhere in the United States and Canada, and offers one-to-one mentoring online. She writes regularly for Lion's Roar and Tricycle, shares recorded talks and guided meditations freely, and as a painter and photographer brings a contemplative eye to her art.

courses.title: The Seven Factors of Awakening with Lisa Ernst and Trudy Goodman
courses.description: A five-day hybrid retreat at Big Bear Retreat Center in the mountains of southern California, which can be joined in person or online. With Trudy Goodman she works through the seven qualities the Buddha named as supports for awakening, from mindfulness and investigation to joy, calm and equanimity, through practice, talks and dialogue.

courses.title: Intimate with Life: Bethany Hills December Retreat
courses.description: A silent residential retreat at Bethany Hills in Kingston Springs, a short drive west of Nashville, lasting three nights with an option to stay for five. Days move between sitting and walking practice, instruction and evening talks, starting with breath and body and widening into open awareness and compassion. It is open to newcomers and long-term meditators alike.

courses.title: Monday Night Meditation at One Dharma Nashville
courses.description: The community's main weekly gathering, usually led by Lisa, with a period of sitting, a dharma talk and time for questions, closing with a short compassion practice. It meets in person in Nashville and on Zoom, and all levels are welcome.

courses.title: One-to-One Meditation Guidance and Mentoring
courses.description: Individual hour-long sessions on Zoom for people who want personal guidance in building or deepening a Buddhist meditation practice and carrying it into daily life. She works with all levels but mainly with intermediate and experienced meditators.

free_resources.title: How to Love Yourself
free_resources.description: An article in Lion's Roar on metta, or lovingkindness, and why offering it to ourselves first is so often the hardest step. She draws on her own early experience of the practice and gives a way into it.

free_resources.title: Your Deepest Questions
free_resources.description: A Lion's Roar piece that begins with a strict Zen retreat and her first koan, and explores how sitting with an open question, rather than reaching for an answer, can become a practice in itself.

free_resources.title: A Selection of Dharma Talks and Guided Meditations
free_resources.description: Her own page gathering free recordings of recent dharma talks and guided meditations on lovingkindness, equanimity, self-compassion and spacious awareness, alongside links to her published articles.
